newsitem.title: UK: IRA bomb victim dies - police.
newsitem.headline: IRA bomb victim dies - police.

text.p: A soldier injured in a double IRA bombing of Britain's army headquarters in Northern Ireland has died, police said on Friday.
The British soldier was one of 31 people injured in the attack on Monday, the Irish Republican Army's first in the province for two years.
"A soldier has died this morning," a police spokeswoman told Reuters.

Irish Republican Army (IRA) bombers infiltrated high security at the army base to plant the bombs, timed to go off 20 minutes apart so that rescue services and victims of the first blast would be caught in the second.
The bombs were a severe blow to Northern Ireland peace efforts, raising fears that pro-British Loyalist guerrillas would retaliate by ending their two-year ceasefire.
The IRA had called off its own 17-month truce on February 9 and set off a series of bombs on the British mainland, but had not attacked Northern Ireland until this week.
